rationale: The workflow already implements the two evidence-supported optimizations that are relevant to it. Dependency downloads are cached via ruby/setup-ruby with bundler-cache: true (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE: cache dependency downloads), and superseded in-progress runs are cancelled via concurrency.group with cancel-in-progress: true (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE: cancel superseded runs). No other pattern applies cleanly: there is no matrix (so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST do not apply), no schedule (so P-LIT-FAIL-SCHEDULE, P-LIT-IDLE-SCHEDULE do not apply), no test suite to select or prioritize, no Bazel build, and no duration history is available in ci_history to justify a custom timeout (P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT / P-LIT-HISTORY-TIMEOUT) without risking false timeouts on valid slow runs. Path filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) and run skipping (P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW) have limited reported impact and could alter required deploy coverage, so they are not suitable minimal changes. Adding a redundant explicit actions/cache for Bundler would duplicate bundler-cache: true and is unsupported as a clear benefit (the related experiment showed elapsed savings but slightly increased job runtime and is labelled experimental, not a recommendation).
